title: Optimal Conditional-Median Policy Value under Vanishing Overlap and Median Density
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=subfield < floor=field (target=field) and NOT salvageable in scope
gap_reasons: D0.5.G tier=subfield < floor=field (target=field) and NOT salvageable in scope

The contribution is confined to a highly calibrated one-dimensional class with uniform covariates, an exactly known power propensity, an anchored Lipschitz median, and fixed quadratic-crossing constants, while the critical gamma=5 case, subcritical regime, unknown propensity, and adaptation remain open.

The proposed interval is only order-optimal, uses a very conservative Markov calibration, and can equal the full parameter range at practically relevant sample sizes, with no numerical study establishing usable constants.

The lower-length proof imports the proof-local κ_γ/v_γ KL-to-TV calculation from thm:gamma-risk-frontier, but that theorem statement supplies neither; derive it locally from lem:gamma-signed-experiment or expose it as a stated lemma.
The γ=6 corollary asserts Q_{6,0}=Q_0 without either signed-law construction among its declared dependencies; add the constructions or a stated specialization lemma.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived matched minimax absolute-error and honest connected-interval length rates for each fixed known propensity exponent γ>5, including n^(-2/11) at γ=6. D0.5 graded the delivered note subfield, below the required field floor, because its calibrated model, conservative interval, and unresolved critical/adaptive regimes limit the contribution. The reviewers also identified two local dependency-closure defects in the length proof and γ=6 corollary; the sound research record is retained for a future re-raise.
tldr: For every fixed boundary-overlap exponent \(\gamma>5\), the optimal average conditional-median policy value is point identified but has matched minimax expected absolute error and uniformly \(95\%\)-honest connected-interval expected length of order \(n^{-2/(\gamma+5)}\). A single observed-data dyadic binned-median estimator and conservative interval attain the upper order, while one continuous mean-preserving signed experiment gives both lower bounds and leaves both marginal potential-outcome laws unchanged. The original \(e(x)=x^6/2\) results remain as the named \(\gamma=6\) corollaries with rate \(n^{-2/11}\).
gap: Regular conditional-median value theory divides by both the propensity and the density at the median, while weak-overlap quantile theory treats marginal potential-outcome quantiles and weak-overlap minimax theory treats linear conditional-mean functionals. None of the inspected results covers a positive-part integral of a moving conditional median when both denominators lose uniform lower bounds.
fill: The project derives the resulting \(h=n^{-1/11}\) modulus, matches it with a fully observed-data dyadic estimator, transfers the same obstruction to honest interval length, and exhibits a lower pair invisible to every marginal potential-outcome quantile and every conditional mean.
